summary: Structured semantic controlled-contract authoring, task-complete proof selection and coverage authoring, bounded assessment queries, integration-test-design assessment, and deterministic private-scope census tools. Server ownership protects canonical identity, currentness, and mutation integrity rather than secrecy; registered routes expose no raw carrier bytes or generic content-reference fallback.

tools.notes: Thin bounded query over the package-owned vocabulary. The result is advisory authoring assistance and never runtime truth, readiness, authorization, or policy.

Lists or searches all package-owned controlled proof intents through the bounded library API. Query length is package-measured in UTF-8 bytes with a 1024-byte maximum and package-owned bounded smaller-query recovery. It performs no pack selection, invocation, admission, or authority decision.
use_when: The controlled proof intent remains semantically unknown after the caller provides its task or query.
do_not_use_when: Exact controlled proof intent IDs are known; use workspace_controlled_proof_packs_select.
authoritative_for: bounded discovery of package-owned controlled proof intent identities

recommended_first_call.operation: discover an unknown controlled proof intent

tools.notes: Selects package-owned proof packs for explicit intent IDs and returns canonical WK/focus context, exact inspection calls, and bounded transport. It performs no invocation, admission, policy, or lifecycle decision.
use_when: A caller needs the decision state, compatible exact candidate identities, unresolved authoring inputs, and callable inspections for explicit controlled proof intents.
do_not_use_when: The caller needs unrelated contract or proof-pack populations, raw package results, paths, carrier bytes, admission, authorization, certification, or CCE decisions.

tools.notes: Authoring projection for one exact package-owned pack identity. It accepts no profile path, package root, module, executable, catalog, cwd, or environment override.

Compact-first selector-aware binding assistance. Omitted evaluation_focus uses no input, null selects the canonical root carrier, and a canonical lowercase slug of at most 128 UTF-8 bytes selects a focused carrier; invalid focus refuses before path resolution. Role/status pages are digest-bound and compatible candidates remain unselected and non-authoritative.

Orchestrator/operator compilation from server-resolved canonical carriers through the package buildProofPlan export. It validates the complete supplied binding set without enumerating the independently bounded binding-assistance candidate projection, then CAS-writes only the deterministic proof-plan carrier.

Planning-only. One final-envelope owner returns a bounded non-authoritative task-relevant summary with assessment_identity, exact counts and omissions, and typed continuation through workspace_controlled_contract_assessment_query. It exposes no raw carriers or source-derived detail, result, population, or requirement digests.
use_when: A caller needs a deterministic planning assessment of one canonical contract and persisted proof plan.
do_not_use_when: The caller needs runtime test execution, raw carriers, filesystem paths, persistence, or lifecycle authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: assess canonical contract and proof plan

tools.notes: Queries one task-relevant proof-assessment collection. Authenticated cursors continue rows and typed fields; oversized scalars use offset/length ranges with exact total. Identity, currentness, and expiry bind each page. No raw carrier, artifact, spill, persistence, or lifecycle authority.
use_when: A caller needs bounded semantic detail from a live proof assessment snapshot.
do_not_use_when: The caller needs raw carrier, proof artifact, filesystem path, persistence, spill, or lifecycle access.

tools.notes: Executable targets resolve only from exact acceptance.validation[] {operation: node_test, target, verification_ids} declarations through the shared wiki-core owner; strings and {note, verification_ids} objects are inert. Public results contain only the requested subject, one common subject-binding summary, aggregate status/counts, compact proof and verification identity/status rows, and minimal reason/recovery facts for non-satisfied outcomes. structuredContent never exceeds 65,536 UTF-8 bytes and never exposes inventories, output, stacks, absolute paths, commands, argv, environment, or raw runtime payloads.
use_when: An orchestrator or operator needs runtime proof for one exact integrated controlled-contract implementation slice.
do_not_use_when: The subject is a whole WK, the slice is not integrated, or the caller needs planning assessment, proof authoring, admission, or lifecycle authority.
tools.notes: Post-integration orchestrator/operator route for proving one exact integrated implementation slice; a whole-WK subject is refused. Caller input is only { repo?, unit, focus? }. Side effects are process_spawn and workspace_write. The route resolves the canonical slice lifecycle and launcher-owned fixed fork/tip, creates one private mode-0700 detached checkout at that tip, runs the declared candidate, falsifier, and traversal population through the launcher-owned provider, validates every authenticated runtime-evidence receipt, and returns a runtime-scoped, non-authoritative assessment. Caller-supplied lifecycle, Git, path, command, environment, provider, receipt, witness, assessment, or authority fields are refused rather than overridden. Lifecycle, population, provider, receipt, or assessment failure returns a typed refusal, never a planning assessment; this route never calls workspace_controlled_contract_assess. It is not a proof-pack authoring, selection, assessment, admission, or authority surface and grants no admission, certification, CCE, or dispatch outcome.

recommended_first_call.operation: prove one integrated controlled-contract slice at runtime

use_when: An authenticated orchestrator must verify the complete proof population selected by one canonical WK, slice, test-proof, or obligation subject against the configured clean or dirty worktree, or against a shared authenticated private detached materialization of an exact full Git commit.
An eligible launcher-managed worker or reviewer must execute every exact server-resolved declared test proof selected by one canonical subject.
do_not_use_when: A managed worker or reviewer wants to supply git_sha or escape its launcher-bound candidate.
The task needs a caller-selected path, command, target, environment, provider, evaluator, receipt, policy, authority, arbitrary test execution, replay authority, or lifecycle authority.
authoritative_for: advisory satisfied, unsatisfied, not_executable, or typed-refusal verification of one deterministic, completely preflighted proof population with canonical relationship projection, authenticated selected-worktree facts, confined execution, receipt, proof-pack, and evaluator identities

recommended_first_call.operation: verify one canonically selected proof population

tools.notes: Orchestrator/operator expected-absence creation for contract, evaluation-input, and proof-plan-request carriers through package validation; returns no carrier content.

use_when: A caller needs a bounded index or selective stable-ID projection of one canonical controlled-contract carrier.
do_not_use_when: The caller needs to mutate a carrier or retrieve an unbounded complete carrier.
tools.notes: Bounded index or selective stable-ID/binding-role projection. Index mode applies the registry-derived carrier target, filter, and cursor vocabulary. A nonempty selectors list selects selected mode and intentionally ignores target, filter, and cursor. Invalid index targets return registry-derived valid targets and retry guidance. It never implicitly returns or spills a complete carrier.
Orchestrator/operator bounded typed domain mutation with prospective package validation and one expected-digest CAS write; direct proof-plan mutation is forbidden.

Orchestrator/operator-only atomic stable-v1 verification-bundle mutation. Arguments are repo?, wk_id, focus?, expected_content_digest, and 1..64 complete controlled-contract-verification-bundle.v1 upsert/remove operations. The controlled-contract package owns the bundle shape and required-field population, which this route derives; authoring state emits an operation-ready bundle with server-known identities, attachment relation, target constraints, and provider/version bindings bound. The server resolves the canonical carrier and performs at most one workspace write using digest CAS after package validation. Caller paths and authority carriers are not accepted, and the route confers no authority beyond that validated mutation.

Package-backed compact schema, identity, mutability, and minimal-template projection for one carrier kind and optional target; complete schemas and proof corpora remain out of default discovery responses.

Read-only task-directed state for same-WK carriers. Inputs are repo?, wk_id, focus?, and continuation?. The state owner solely defines the stage vocabulary and exactly-one-next-action-or-stop invariant. Valid published root, focused, and existing-request continuations settle directly at proof_plan_ready; no carrier-conflict recovery hop is valid. Results are bounded, omit carrier and candidate populations, and confer no mutation, admission, or policy authority.
use_when: A coordinator needs the canonical next authoring action or direct settled state for same-WK carriers.
do_not_use_when: The caller intends to supply source declarations or filesystem authority; canonical source state is server-owned.
The intent is to mutate carriers or publish a proof graph; this route is read-only.

tools.notes: Atomic orchestrator/operator publication of the server-held proof graph. Inputs are repo?, wk_id, focus?, and one server-issued continuation; no caller proposal or source declaration is accepted. The exact source declaration is server-owned and derived from authenticated canonical state. Valid root, focused, and existing-request continuations next settle directly at proof_plan_ready. No admission or policy authority is granted.
use_when: A coordinator holds the exact server-issued continuation for a complete proof-graph proposal and needs atomic publication.
do_not_use_when: The caller intends to supply a proposal, source declaration, path, environment, persistence carrier, or other authority input.
Server composition still reports unresolved pointers; controlled_contract_proof_graph_proposal_incomplete describes only that reachable state.
The proposal still needs author semantics; return to the exact authoring-state next action.

tools.notes: Read-only orchestrator/operator route for package-backed proof skeleton generation. Supply repo?, wk_id, focus?, one exact selected_pack, explicit requested_intents, exactly one of caller bindings or evaluation_input, and optionally a proposal_draft containing only carrier_operations. The exact source declaration is server-owned and derived from authenticated canonical state; the public schema accepts no caller source declaration. The server derives evaluation-input basenames, composes the canonical selected-pack population, mints continuation identities, and returns one next action. Continuation-integrity failures remain typed and distinct. Results confer no mutation, admission, or policy authority. See docs/mcp-operation-reference.md for the exact taxonomy.
use_when: A coordinator needs the package-owned evaluation-input and composed proof-plan-request skeleton for one exact admitted pack before authoring proof carriers.
do_not_use_when: The caller intends to supply carrier paths, basenames, or any other filesystem authority; every canonical path is server-resolved from wk_id and focus.
The intent is to mutate, admit, or integrate a carrier; this route projects a skeleton and confers no mutation, admission, or policy authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: project one skeleton from an exact admitted pack

tools.notes: Orchestrator/operator-only mixed-effect common proof capture over one server-resolved repository alias, canonical WK and unit, optional canonical focus, one of behavioral_preservation, declared_boundary_consistency, test_verification_validity, or write_confinement, exact profile identity, and optional verification identity. Behavioral-preservation, test-verification-validity, and write-confinement are read-only joins over launcher-owned receipts through the optional private resolver; when that resolver is unavailable they return a typed prerequisite refusal. Declared-boundary-consistency instead resolves canonical repository inputs and may atomically publish its canonical carrier. Integration-prefix is deliberately absent because workspace_controlled_integration_prefix_capture_author remains its owner. The route accepts no roots, paths, receipt payloads, reports, policies, commits, executors, resolvers, continuations, or authority digests. Results are advisory and make no admission, certification, CCE, dispatch, review, or proof-authority decision.

Orchestrator/operator-only canonical integration-prefix capture authoring. Arguments are wk_id, optional canonical focus, and optional exact proof.integration.prefix-safety@1.0.0 profile selectors; repository identity, carriers, complete populations, graph inputs, filesystem paths, source digests, writer authority, and completeness are server-resolved and cannot be supplied by the caller. The wiki-core controlled authoring operation owns package invocation, the live source lease, atomic carrier-set publication, validation, and typed failures. Success returns integration-prefix-capture-authoring-receipt-v1 with identity, generation and manifest digests, complete counts, and bound digests, bounded to 8192 UTF-8 bytes; overflow fails loudly without returning an inline population.

do_not_use_when: No valid server-issued continuation is available, or the caller only needs to inspect authoring state.
tools.notes: Orchestrator/operator continuation mutation. Arguments are repo?, wk_id, focus?, one server-issued continuation identity, and optional returned expected_stage. It validates WK, focus, contract, package continuation, stage, and canonical carrier state before one expected-absence CAS write; recoverable refusals return a state-derived replacement call.
Package-derived stable-v1 test-proof binding contract, provider-registry identity, compatibility rules, and authoring limits.
Bounded selective stable-v1 package validation by exact same-WK verification identity; experimental and mixed families refuse.
Orchestrator/operator package-validated typed test-proof binding mutation with stale-digest refusal and one digest-CAS write.
